I have been farming these 35 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years now. At 63, with my agricultural college background, I understand the science, but I also know this specific soil. My wife and I are the only ones at home — our children work in Shijiazhuang — so every decision has to account for our labor limits. I am not getting younger, and hiring labor now costs 120 yuan per day, so I have trimmed my cotton area down to 5 mu over the years. The remaining 30 mu stays in the wheat-maize double crop. It is reliable, mechanized for the most part, and fits what two people can manage.

It is early April now. The winter wheat I planted last October is greening up well after the winter irrigation I gave it in March. I am targeting about 470 kg/mu this year — last year I got 450, but the soil moisture profile looks better this spring. For the wheat, I already put down base fertilizer in October: about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer and 15 kg of DAP. Now I am planning the jointing topdress — I will spread roughly 20 kg of urea per mu in mid-April. Total N for the wheat comes to about 16 kg/mu, which is the rate I have settled on after decades of watching the response on this field. I will irrigate four times total: the winter irrigation is already done, and now I need to hit jointing, heading, and grain filling. Electricity for the pump is not cheap, so I time each irrigation to the growth stage and skip it if we get decent rain. I will spray once for weeds and once for powdery mildew if it shows up.

After wheat harvest in early June, the window to get maize in is tight — sometimes five to seven days. I use minimal tillage and direct seeding with the planter to save time. I am planting a hybrid variety, about 50 yuan per mu for seed. I band compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at the 8-10 leaf stage in early July, for a total of about 15 kg N/mu. Three irrigations: jointing, tasseling, and grain filling if September turns dry. Yield target is 510 kg/mu. I could push the N higher, but at my age I have learned that the last few kilograms rarely pay for themselves.

I keep 5 mu of cotton because the price has been stable and I know the technology, but it is labor-intensive. I plant a hybrid in late April after plowing and harrowing that plot. I apply base fertilizer before planting — compound plus a bit of DAP — and topdress urea at flowering in July. Two irrigations, at flowering and boll setting. I expect about 240 kg/mu. I will need to hire pickers for three days per mu come September and October, which adds up, but 5 mu is manageable for us.

The total input cost this year will run about 26,000 yuan. That is a significant outlay for a farm our size, but I bought fertilizer early when prices were slightly lower, and I have enough cash on hand. At 63, I do not gamble on new varieties or untested methods across the whole farm — if something looks promising, I try it on half a mu first.
